findings.title: List datasets with mismatched columns are silently widened to the column union and filled with invented data
findings.description: Imputer.fit/_stack uses pd.concat(datasets, axis=0, ignore_index=True). When list datasets do not share columns (documented requirement in common.py: 'which must share columns' -- but never validated), concat takes the column UNION, creating all-NaN blocks that the imputer then 'fills'. Every returned dataset is widened to the union width: a dataset that never had column 'z' comes back with a fabricated constant 'z' column equal to the OTHER dataset's column mean. Output shapes do not match input shapes, contradicting the impute() docstring ('split back into a list matching the input structure'). Plain arrays of different widths (the canonical multi-subject hyperalignment case, which hypertools explicitly supports elsewhere -- see format_data's QC comment 'datasets can legitimately have DIFFERENT column counts') hit the same path, including inside hyp.plot: hyp.plot([50x3, 50x5] with NaNs) silently widens the 3-column subject to 5 columns with phantom mean-filled data before alignment. No error, no warning.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(3)
la = pd.DataFrame(rng.randn(12, 4) + 5, columns=list('wxyz')); la.iloc[3, 1] = np.nan
c = pd.DataFrame(rng.randn(10, 3) - 5, columns=list('wxy')); c.iloc[2, 0] = np.nan
res = hyp.impute([la, c], model='SimpleImputer')
print([r.shape for r in res])          # [(12, 4), (10, 4)] -- second dataset widened
print(np.asarray(res[1])[:4, -1])      # constant 4.556... = mean of la['z']
res2 = hyp.impute([rng.randn(10, 3), rng.randn(10, 4)], model='SimpleImputer')
print([r.shape for r in res2])         # [(10, 4), (10, 4)]
findings.expected: Either a clear ValueError ('datasets in a list must share columns; got ...') or per-dataset handling; output list shapes must match input shapes.
findings.actual:
A: DataFrames wxyz + wxy -> [(12, 4), (10, 4)]
   ds1 z-column (never existed) values[:4]: [4.556 4.556 4.556 4.556]
   -> invented column filled with ds0-only stats: True
B: arrays (10,3)+(10,4) -> [(10, 4), (10, 4)]
F: plot mixed-width NaN datasets -> OK Figure (silent)

findings.title: Default PPCA (d=None -> full rank) imputation degenerates to ~column-mean fill; recovery r=0.13 where d=3 gives r=0.98
findings.description: With the default d=None, external ppca uses d = n_columns (full rank). On 120x8 rank-3 data with 10% MCAR holes, the imputed entries are numerically indistinguishable from plain column means (max |imputed - column_mean| = 2.2e-4) and correlate with ground truth at r=+0.1251 -- identical to SimpleImputer's mean fill (r=+0.1251, same rmse to 4 decimals). Setting d=3 (the true rank) yields r=+0.9764, proving the machinery works when d is a bottleneck. On a smooth timeseries PPCA default gives r=+0.1561 vs Kalman +0.9981 / KNN +0.9949. PPCA is the DEFAULT imputer for hyp.impute AND the default NaN path of hyp.plot/format_data, so out-of-the-box missing-data handling is effectively mean imputation dressed up as PPCA (plus a misleading non-convergence warning, see -004). At 40% missing it does better (r=+0.6895) but still below IterativeImputer (+0.8696). No docs mention that d must be set below n_columns for PPCA to reconstruct anything.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
n, d, r = 120, 8, 3
truth = rng.randn(n, r) @ rng.randn(r, d) + 0.05 * rng.randn(n, d)
holes = rng.rand(n, d) < 0.10
for i in range(n):
    if holes[i].all(): holes[i, rng.randint(d)] = False
x = truth.copy(); x[holes] = np.nan
mean_fill = np.broadcast_to(np.nanmean(x, axis=0), x.shape)
out = np.asarray(hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='PPCA'))
print(np.max(np.abs(out[holes] - mean_fill[holes])))   # ~2e-4
print(np.corrcoef(out[holes], truth[holes])[0, 1])     # ~0.13
out3 = np.asarray(hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='PPCA', d=3))
print(np.corrcoef(out3[holes], truth[holes])[0, 1])    # ~0.98
findings.expected: Default PPCA should recover low-rank structure (r >> mean fill), or the default d should be chosen < n_columns (e.g. via variance criterion), or docs should state that d must be set for meaningful reconstruction.
findings.actual:
(a) PPCA default d=None, 10% missing: 0/91 imputed entries EXACTLY equal column mean; max|imputed-mean|=2.185e-04
(b) PPCA d=3: r=+0.9764 rmse=0.3750
t01 10%: PPCA r=+0.1251 rmse=1.4992 == SimpleImputer r=+0.1251 rmse=1.4992

findings.title: PPCA imputation is nondeterministic (unseeded np.random.randn init) and random_state= is silently ignored
findings.description: external/ppca.py fit() initializes C = np.random.randn(D, d) from the GLOBAL numpy RNG with no seed parameter. Two identical hyp.impute(x, model='PPCA') calls return different imputed values (max diff 3.8e-4 default-d, 5.9e-5 d=3 on the t03 data); reproducibility requires setting global np.random.seed before every call. Passing random_state=0 to hyp.impute is accepted without error but silently ignored for PPCA (kwargs are forwarded to fitter which only reads d/min_obs/tol). For a reproducible-science library whose plot() explicitly threads random_state into reduce/cluster stages, the default imputer being unseedable is a trap. (IterativeImputer's random_state works: verified deterministic.)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
truth = rng.randn(120, 3) @ rng.randn(3, 8) + 0.05 * rng.randn(120, 8)
holes = rng.rand(120, 8) < 0.10
x = truth.copy(); x[holes] = np.nan
a = np.asarray(hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='PPCA'))
b = np.asarray(hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='PPCA'))
print(np.array_equal(a, b))  # False
c = hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='PPCA', random_state=0)  # accepted, silently ignored
findings.expected: PPCA accepts and honors a random_state/seed parameter (or seeds deterministically); unknown kwargs are rejected or warned about.
findings.actual:
default d: identical = False  max diff at imputed = 0.0003840091728770645
d=3      : identical = False  max diff at imputed = 5.930465746617486e-05
with np.random.seed(123) before each call: identical = True
random_state kwarg: accepted (no error)

findings.title: Full-rank PPCA EM routinely hits the 500-iteration bound and warns 'did not converge (relative change nan)' -- including in the shipped gallery example; a zero-variance column collapses the whole reconstruction to mean-fill
findings.description: With default d=None, the EM convergence criterion plateaus (~2e-3 > tol 1e-4) on ordinary dense data, so users regularly see 'PPCA EM did not converge within 500 iterations ...; Results may be approximate' on clean inputs -- including hyp.plot of NaN data and examples/plot_impute.py run verbatim (where the relative change is reported as nan, i.e. the objective went non-finite because of the fully-missing rows). A constant (zero-variance) column makes nanstd=0 -> division by zero -> EM diff=nan immediately, burning 500 iterations, and the resulting NaN-poisoned reconstruction means EVERY missing entry in EVERY column falls back to the column-mean splice (verified: PPCA output equals SimpleImputer output exactly on the constant-column dataset). Whether the warning fires is also nondeterministic run-to-run (see -003): the same t01/t02 call produced no warning in one process and the warning in another.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
base = rng.randn(40, 4) * 2 + 1
cst = base.copy(); cst[:, 3] = 7.0; cst[4, 3] = np.nan; cst[6, 0] = np.nan
out = hyp.impute(cst, model='PPCA')  # warns 'last relative change nan'; [6,0] == column mean
# and: MPLBACKEND=Agg python examples/plot_impute.py  (same warning, 'relative change nan')
findings.expected: No scary non-convergence warning on ordinary data; zero-variance columns handled (epsilon-guard or drop) without poisoning the EM objective for all columns.
findings.actual:
[constant col / PPCA] warn: PPCA EM did not converge within 500 iterations (last relative change nan, tol 0.0001); [4,3] -> 7.0; [6,0] -> 0.828 (== column mean, same as SimpleImputer)
t07 gallery example verbatim: 'PPCA EM did not converge within 500 iterations (last relative change nan, tol 0.0001); returning the current e...'

findings.title: Reusing a fitted PPCA imputer on data with a different column count raises a cryptic IndexError; the documented ValueError is unreachable
findings.description: ppca.transformer's new-data path slices original[:, valid] BEFORE the friendly column-count check, where `valid` is the fit-time boolean mask. Any column-count mismatch makes the boolean slice itself raise 'IndexError: boolean index did not match indexed array along axis 1', so the guard on the next line ('PPCA.transform on new data requires the same columns...' -- and the docstring's promised 'Raises ValueError If data has a different number of columns') is dead code.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(2)
train = rng.randn(60, 4) * 3 + 10; train[rng.rand(60, 4) < 0.1] = np.nan
_, mp = hyp.impute(train, model='PPCA', d=2, return_model=True)
hyp.impute(rng.randn(10, 7), model=mp)  # IndexError, not the documented ValueError
findings.expected: ValueError: 'PPCA.transform on new data requires the same columns the imputer was fit on ...' (per hypertools/impute/ppca.py docstring)
findings.actual: [PPCA reuse wrong n_cols] IndexError: boolean index did not match indexed array along axis 1; size of axis is 7 but size of corresponding boolean axis is 4

findings.title: ppca.py module docstring contradicts the implementation: it claims non-missing entries are NOT preserved, but the splice preserves them byte-identically; format_data's 'Inexact solution' warning is equally stale
findings.description: hypertools/impute/ppca.py module docstring: 'Unlike the other imputers in this package, PPCA does not merely replace missing entries: ... non-missing entries are NOT guaranteed to be preserved exactly ... use SimpleImputer/KNNImputer/IterativeImputer/Kalman for exact preservation of non-missing values.' The transformer code directly below it does the opposite (SPLICE comment: 'keep every observed (non-NaN) value exactly and fill ONLY the missing positions'), and t01 verified observed entries are byte-identical (max_obs_diff=0.00e+00 at 10% and 40% missing). Related stale text on the hyp.plot default path: format_data warns 'Missing data: Inexact solution computed with PPCA (see https://github.com/allentran/pca-magic for details)' -- observed data now pass through exactly, and only missing entries are approximate; plot.py's impute docstring claim 'default: None, i.e. PPCA -- byte-compatible with pre-1.0 behavior' is likewise inconsistent with the QC comment in ppca.py that the pre-1.0 output ('m.transform() = latent PCA scores') was deliberately replaced by the splice.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python t01_models_mcar.py  # PPCA observed_exact=True max_obs_diff=0.00e+00 at 10% and 40%
findings.expected: Module docstring describes the actual splice behavior; format_data warning and plot.py docstring updated to match.
findings.actual: Docstring: 'non-missing entries are NOT guaranteed to be preserved exactly'; measured: PPCA observed_exact=True max_obs_diff=0.00e+00 (both missingness levels); plot warning verbatim: 'Missing data: Inexact solution computed with PPCA (see https://github.'

findings.title: kwargs handling is inconsistent across model-spec forms, and unknown/typo'd kwargs are always silently swallowed
findings.description: Outer **kwargs are applied for string/class specs and MERGED into the deprecated {'model','params'} dict form, but silently DROPPED for the canonical {'model','args','kwargs'} dict form (impute.py line ~94 instantiates cls(*args, **resolved_kwargs) without merging the outer kwargs) and silently ignored for instance specs (documented, but without any warning). Worse, every imputer constructor accepts **kwargs and fitters read parameters via kwargs.get, so a typo'd parameter name is silently ignored: hyp.impute(x, model='SimpleImputer', strateggy='median') runs with strategy='mean' -- the user believes they imputed with the median. Same mechanism silently swallows random_state for PPCA (see -003).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(2); x = rng.randn(40, 4); x[5, 2] = np.nan
r3 = hyp.impute(x.copy(), model={'model': 'SimpleImputer', 'kwargs': {}}, strategy='constant', fill_value=-99.0)
print(np.asarray(r3)[5, 2])  # NOT -99.0 (outer kwargs dropped)
r4 = hyp.impute(x.copy(), model={'model': 'SimpleImputer', 'params': {}}, strategy='constant', fill_value=-99.0)
print(np.asarray(r4)[5, 2])  # -99.0 (merged)
r8 = hyp.impute(x.copy(), model='SimpleImputer', strateggy='median')  # typo: silently mean
findings.expected: Consistent kwargs merging across spec forms; unknown constructor kwargs raise TypeError or warn.
findings.actual:
outer kwargs w/ kwargs-form dict: imputed=-0.071 (constant applied: False)
outer kwargs w/ params-form dict: imputed=-99.000 (constant applied: True)
instance + kwargs: kwargs ignored: True (no warning)
typo kwarg strateggy=median: no error, imputed=-0.07062 (mean=-0.07062 median=-0.16396)

findings.title: Degenerate inputs produce cryptic or bizarre errors: None/empty -> sklearn internals, [] -> loads the 'minipedia' text corpus, all-NaN + PPCA -> 'zero-size array to reduction'; Imputer.fit uses assert (AssertionError instead of documented ValueError)
findings.description: hyp.impute(None) and hyp.impute(np.empty((0,3))) raise sklearn's 'Found array with 0 sample(s) ... while a minimum of 1 is required by SimpleImputer'. hyp.impute([]) is routed down datawrangler's TEXT pipeline: it prints 'loading corpus: minipedia...done!' (loading a text corpus for an empty list!) then fails with 'Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) ... required by LatentDirichletAllocation'. hyp.impute(all-NaN array, model='PPCA') raises 'ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity'. format_data has friendly messages for these exact situations ('input has no observations (0 rows)...', 'input is entirely missing (all values are NaN)...') but standalone hyp.impute lacks them. Additionally Imputer.fit's own guard is 'assert data is not None, ValueError(...)' -- it raises AssertionError (not the ValueError its docstring documents), and asserts are stripped under python -O; the same assert-with-exception-instance-as-message pattern is used for the fitter-returns-dict checks.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.impute([])                                        # minipedia corpus + LDA error
hyp.impute(None)                                       # sklearn 0-sample error
hyp.impute(np.full((10, 3), np.nan), model='PPCA')     # zero-size reduction error
from hypertools.impute import SimpleImputer
SimpleImputer().fit(None)                              # AssertionError, docstring says ValueError
findings.expected: Clear hypertools-level messages ('input has no observations', 'input is entirely missing', 'cannot impute an empty dataset' as a real ValueError).
findings.actual:
[empty list] loading corpus: minipedia...done! ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.
[None] ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 0)) while a minimum of 1 is required by SimpleImputer.
[all-NaN dataset / PPCA] ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity
fit(None) raises: AssertionError | cannot impute an empty dataset

findings.title: Kalman imputer crashes on single-row input with a raw pykalman broadcast error
findings.description: hyp.impute(np.array([[1.0, np.nan, 3.0]]), model='Kalman') raises 'ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (3,3) into shape (3,1)' from inside pykalman's smoother (kalman_gains[t] frame) -- leaked internals with no hint that Kalman needs multiple timepoints. PPCA on the same input gives an exemplary message ('PPCA needs at least 2 columns with >= min_obs (10) non-missing observations ... Use model="Kalman", "SimpleImputer", or "KNNImputer" ...'). Note PPCA's message recommends Kalman for exactly this case, which then crashes.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.impute(np.array([[1.0, np.nan, 3.0]]), model='Kalman')
findings.expected: Friendly error, e.g. 'Kalman imputation needs at least 2 rows (timepoints); use SimpleImputer for single-row data.'
findings.actual:
[single row / Kalman] RAISED ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (3,3) into shape (3,1)
    last frame:     kalman_gains[t],

findings.title: 1D input is treated as a single ROW (1 x n) and its NaN is filled with 0.0 -- inconsistent with format_data/plot's 1D -> (n, 1) convention
findings.description: hyp.impute(np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0, 4.0]), model='SimpleImputer') returns shape (1, 4) with the NaN replaced by 0.0 (the missing value becomes an all-NaN 'column' of a one-row matrix, zero-filled via keep_empty_features), not the series mean 2.67. hypertools' own format_data/plot reshape 1D input to (n, 1) -- n observations of 1 feature -- so the same vector means different things to hyp.plot and hyp.impute. Also violates the impute() docstring's 'preserving its shape' ((4,) -> (1, 4)). A scientist imputing a 1D timeseries silently gets 0 substituted.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
out = hyp.impute(np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0, 4.0]), model='SimpleImputer')
print(np.asarray(out))  # [[1. 0. 3. 4.]], shape (1, 4)
findings.expected: 1D input treated as (n, 1) like format_data (NaN -> mean of observed series = 2.67), or an explicit error asking for 2D input.

findings.title: List-of-DataFrames input loses each DataFrame's index (reset to RangeIndex); single-DataFrame input preserves it
findings.description: _stack concatenates with ignore_index=True and _split rebuilds parts with pd.DataFrame(p, columns=stacked.columns), dropping per-dataset indexes. A single DataFrame keeps its index and columns through impute (verified), so metadata handling is inconsistent between the single and list paths. Column names ARE preserved for lists.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(2)
la = pd.DataFrame(rng.randn(30, 4), columns=list('wxyz'), index=range(100, 130)); la.iloc[3, 1] = np.nan
lb = pd.DataFrame(rng.randn(25, 4), columns=list('wxyz'), index=range(500, 525)); lb.iloc[10, 2] = np.nan
res = hyp.impute([la, lb], model='SimpleImputer')
print(list(res[0].index)[:4])  # [0, 1, 2, 3] -- original 100..129 lost
findings.expected: Per-dataset indexes restored on split (record them in _stack).
findings.actual: ds0 index preserved: False (got [0, 1, 2, 3]...); ds0 columns preserved: True

findings.title: Error message and docstring steer users toward the DEPRECATED {'model','params'} dict form; non-string invalid specs get terse 'unknown model: X' with no supported-forms hint
findings.description: The unknown-name ValueError ends with "(or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, an Imputer subclass, or an Imputer instance directly)" -- following that advice emits a DeprecationWarning since the params form is deprecated in favor of {'model','args','kwargs'}. The impute() docstring likewise lists the params form first without a deprecation note (while the code warns). Non-string invalid specs (42, np.mean, a raw sklearn imputer class or fitted sklearn instance) raise bare 'ValueError: unknown model: <...>' without listing supported forms; given the deliberate name collision (hypertools.impute.SimpleImputer wraps sklearn.impute.SimpleImputer), 'unknown model: <class sklearn.impute._base.SimpleImputer>' with no pointer to the same-named hypertools wrapper is needlessly confusing. A dict spec missing the 'model' key raises bare KeyError: 'model'.
findings.expected: Error text recommends the canonical args/kwargs dict form; class/instance rejections mention Imputer subclass requirement and the hypertools wrapper of the same name; dict-without-model raises a descriptive ValueError.
findings.actual:
[invalid name banana] ValueError: unknown impute model 'banana'; supported names: PPCA, SimpleImputer, KNNImputer, IterativeImputer, Kalman (or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, an Imputer subclass, or an Imputer instance directly)
[raw sklearn SimpleImputer CLASS] ValueError: unknown model: <class 'sklearn.impute._base.SimpleImputer'>
[dict missing model key] KeyError: 'model'
dict params form: OK, DeprecationWarning=["{'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs':"]

findings.title: dtype not preserved: int64/float32 inputs come back float64 even on the no-NaN passthrough
findings.description: All transformers run to_numpy(dtype=float), so a float32 DataFrame (common for neuroimaging) or an int64 DataFrame with no missing values returns float64. Imputation output being float is inevitable where NaNs existed, but the clean-passthrough case silently upcasts too (doubling memory for float32 data).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
f32 = pd.DataFrame(rng.randn(15, 3).astype(np.float32)); f32.iloc[1, 1] = np.nan
print(hyp.impute(f32, model='SimpleImputer').dtypes.iloc[0])  # float64
idf = pd.DataFrame(rng.randint(0, 9, (12, 3)))
print(hyp.impute(idf, model='SimpleImputer').dtypes.iloc[0])  # float64 (was int64)
findings.expected: Preserve input floating dtype where possible (or document the float64 upcast).
findings.actual: dtypes in: [dtype('int64')] out: [dtype('float64')]; dtype in: float32 out: float64

findings.title: PPCA d larger than the number of columns is silently accepted
findings.description: hyp.impute(x_40x4, model='PPCA', d=999) runs without error or warning (external ppca happily builds a 4x999 loading matrix). An invalid latent dimensionality should be validated with a clear message, as reduce() does for ndims.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(2); x = rng.randn(40, 4); x[5, 2] = np.nan
hyp.impute(x, model='PPCA', d=999)  # no error
findings.expected: ValueError like 'd must be <= number of columns (4); got 999'.

findings.title: Standalone impute lacks format_data's friendly pre-checks (inf, empty, all-NaN) -- inconsistent robustness between the plot path and the direct API
findings.description: format_data fails fast with clear messages for inf ('input contains infinite values; remove or replace them...'), zero rows, and all-NaN input, but the standalone hyp.impute path has none of these: inf reaches sklearn ('Input X contains infinity or a value too large for dtype(float64)') or is silently treated as an observed value by PPCA/Kalman (inf preserved in output; np.ma.masked_invalid even masks it as missing for Kalman's fit while the NaN-only splice keeps it). Porting the same pre-checks (or a shared validator) to hyp.impute would make the two entry points behave consistently.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
infd = rng.randn(40, 4); infd[0, 0] = np.inf; infd[1, 1] = np.nan
hyp.impute(infd.copy(), model='SimpleImputer')  # sklearn: Input X contains infinity...
out = hyp.impute(infd.copy(), model='PPCA')      # runs; inf preserved
findings.expected: hyp.impute raises the same friendly messages format_data does, for the same degenerate inputs.
findings.actual:
[inf+nan / SimpleImputer] RAISED ValueError: Input X contains infinity or a value too large for dtype('float64').
[inf+nan / PPCA] OK -> DataFrame; inf preserved=True
